utterance: Hi Chloe, thanks for coming in. I'm the GP you're seeing today. Before we jump to anything, I'd like to hear a bit more about what's been going on. Can you tell me about the burning when you pass urine — when did it start, and is it every time you go? And are you going more often than usual, or feeling like you need to rush to the toilet?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago, and it happens every time. It stings and burns, and it is worst right at the end of weeing. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out and I have to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I have not seen any blood.

utterance: Also, are you having any pain in your lower tummy, any back or side pain, fever or chills, or feeling sick to your stomach? And any discharge or itching down there, or any chance you could be pregnant?
reply: Just the low ache above my bladder and nothing else, and nothing in my back. I have no fevers or shivers and feel fine apart from this, and I am eating normally and have not been sick. There is nothing like that down there, and I don't think I could be pregnant.

utterance: That's really helpful. A few more quick questions: you mentioned it's happened before — how often have you had this, and when was the last time? Have you taken any antibiotics in the last few months? And are you sexually active, with any new partners recently? Also, any allergies to any medications, including antibiotics?
reply: I had one about two years ago and that is it, and I haven't had any antibiotics this year. I have a boyfriend of about a year and it is just him, and I am not allergic to anything that I know of.

finding: Soft abdomen. Mild suprapubic tenderness. No guarding or rebound. No masses.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Thanks for waiting, Chloe. Here's what I found: your urine test shows signs of infection — lots of white cells and bacteria — and your examination is reassuring: you're well in yourself, no fever, no kidney-area tenderness, and just mild soreness over the bladder. A pregnancy test was negative, which is good. So this looks like a straightforward bladder infection, which fits with your symptoms.

I've prescribed you nitrofurantoin, an antibiotic — one 100 mg capsule four times a day for 5 days, so 20 capsules in total. Take them with food, and try to space them evenly through the day. Finish the whole course even if you feel better. It can make your urine turn a harmless brownish-yellow colour, and it can occasionally cause nausea, so taking it with meals helps.

I've also sent a urine sample to the lab to confirm the exact bacteria and check the antibiotic is the right one — that result takes a couple of days, and I'll let you know if anything needs to change.

Alongside the antibiotics: drink plenty of water, and you can take paracetamol or ibuprofen if the discomfort is bothering you. Avoid holding your urine.

Safety-netting — please get urgent care or call back straight away if you develop fever or chills, pain in your back or side, vomiting, or you start feeling much worse. Also come back or call if you're not improving within 48 hours, or if you get a rash, swelling of your face or lips, or any trouble breathing after the antibiotic, as that could be an allergy.

Does that all make sense? Any questions?
reply: That makes sense, and I am just glad I can get the script so I can get back to work.

utterance: You're all set, Chloe. Have the script filled today and start the antibiotics tonight. If anything changes or you don't improve in a couple of days, give us a call. Take care!
reply: Thanks, I will go straight to the chemist now.
